newsitem.title: ITALY: Di Pietro resignation irrevocable - spokeswoman.
newsitem.headline: Di Pietro resignation irrevocable - spokeswoman.

text.p: A decision by former graft-busting magistrate Antonio Di Pietro to quit as public works minister is irrevocable, his spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Shortly before, Prime Minister Romano Prodi told parliament he would ask Di Pietro, who joined the centre-left government when it was formed in May, to withdraw his resignation.
"The resignation remains absolutely irrevocable," Sonia Mancini told reporters. She said Di Pietro's mood was: "decisively more angry than sad".
The shock announcement that Di Pietro was quitting government followed confirmation that he was the subject of a preliminary investigation by magistrates in the northern town of Brescia.

Newspapers on Thursday said Di Pietro was being probed over alleged irregularities in the way he conducted his inquiries while a member of the elite pool of "Clean Hands" magistrates in Milan that exposed deep corruption in politics.
In his letter of resignation, Di Pietro said he had become the victim of a "pigeon shoot".
